solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Small fairy that is producing number one photo?

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
an elf is a small fairy-like being
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A tiny fairy is responsible for the top photograph in some ranking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' looks like a chart position, but it means oneself: the photo is of yourself, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfie is a photograph a person takes of themselves, and 'number one' is slang for oneself.

clue.text: Starter of pork to feature in excellent meal

indicators.note: a starter comes first, so only the opening letter of the meat is kept
to feature in something is to appear inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: the opening letter of pork
super means excellent

explanation.surface: A pork starter is to form part of a fine dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' and 'meal' together suggest a menu, but the starter is just the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Supper is an evening meal, often a light one.

clue.text: Help Dan handle rocks

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes violently, so the letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Aid Dan in coping with a load of stones.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend a hand is an idiom meaning to assist someone.

clue.text: Picturesque scene with some untidy llamas

indicators.note: some means only part, so the answer is a run of letters inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A pretty rural view featuring a few scruffy llamas.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a charming, peaceful pastoral scene, often depicted in poetry or painting.

clue.text: Seafood and beef mentioned in conversation

indicators.note: something mentioned in conversation is spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the clue word rather than one spelt like it

blocks.note: beef is informal for muscle or brawn

explanation.surface: Someone chatting about surf and turf: shellfish and steak come up in talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A mussel is an edible bivalve shellfish, one kind of seafood.

clue.text: Relative on a road, initially, that's foggy

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word before it is kept

blocks.note: an uncle is a relative
taken as written
the opening letter of road

explanation.surface: A family member on a road at the start of a misty journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Foggy in its figurative sense means vague or muddled, not clear in meaning.

clue.text: Hit the slopes and almost lose control

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the phrase's word is dropped

blocks.note: a vehicle that skids slides out of control

explanation.surface: Going skiing and very nearly losing control on the snow.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit the slopes is an idiom for going skiing on mountain runs.

clue.text: Male gender, partially a myth?

indicators.note: partially means in part, so the answer is a stretch of letters within the neighbouring words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Asking whether masculinity is, in part, a fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional story, often not historically true, much like a myth.

clue.text: Stinginess that makes party arty?

blocks.note: surface reading: some quality that turns a gathering into an artistic affair
setter's reading: P, the abbreviation for a penny, is stolen from the front of party, leaving arty

explanation.surface: Asking what kind of meanness could turn a party into something arty.
explanation.walkthrough: P stands for penny in British money; nicking it from 'party' leaves 'arty', a literal picture of the hyphenated answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being mean with money, unwilling to spend even small coins, is a colloquial term for stinginess.

clue.text: Uncomfortable allies ate messily

indicators.note: something done messily is in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Friends who ate untidily leave everyone feeling awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill at ease is an idiom for feeling awkward, uneasy or embarrassed.

clue.text: Citrus fruit returned without a message

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the fruit is read from right to left
in its old sense 'without' means outside, so the turned word sits around the next piece

blocks.note: a lime is a green citrus fruit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lime sent back, apparently with no note attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside, so EMIL wraps around A to give EMAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: An email is an electronic message sent between computers.

clue.text: Get some rest, being terribly idle now

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters that follow are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to someone so lazy at present that they might as well go to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie down is to recline, usually in order to have a nap or recover.

clue.text: Ship's latrine OK after turbulence

indicators.note: turbulence is violent disturbance, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The vessel's toilet survived a rough voyage intact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ship's' reads as possessive, but it is 'Ship is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil tanker is a large vessel built to carry petroleum in bulk.

clue.text: Tune Laura played in the nude

indicators.note: a piece that is played is performed or toyed with, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Laura performs a melody while wearing nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Au naturel is a French borrowing meaning naked, in a natural state.

clue.text: Take care of uniform return somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters can be arranged differently

blocks.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to look after the return of a uniform in some way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' looks like a reversal signal but is plain fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurture is to look after and encourage the growth of someone or something.

clue.text: Breakfast item that's a load of rubbish?

blocks.note: first meaning: a crisp grid-patterned batter cake
second meaning: long-winded empty talk or writing

explanation.surface: Complaining about a disappointing breakfast dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a gridded batter cake and also verbose, meaningless talk, i.e. nonsense.

clue.text: Piece of cake and cheeses for the audience

indicators.note: an audience listens, so the word is chosen for how it sounds rather than how it is spelt

blocks.note: Brie is a soft French cheese, plural bries

explanation.surface: Cake and cheese being served up to a theatre audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece of cake' looks like food alongside the cheese, but it is the idiom for something easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a breeze and a piece of cake are informal terms for a task that is very easy.

clue.text: Choice beginning to rattle a small country?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: 'and/or' expresses a choice between options, either or both
the opening letter of rattle
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a choice to start rattling things counts as a little nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choice' must be read as the phrase and/or, written without the slash.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a tiny principality in the Pyrenees between France and Spain, one of Europe's smallest states.

clue.text: Style of primarily feeble hideaway

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of feeble
a lair is a den or hiding place

explanation.surface: Describing the look of a rather weak retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair can mean stylishness or elegant panache as well as natural talent.

clue.text: Disregard loud yobbo

blocks.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
a yobbo is British slang for a rowdy, uncouth youth, a lout

explanation.surface: Ignoring a noisy hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: To flout a rule is to openly ignore or defy it.

clue.text: Biscuit you'll get a lot out of?

definitions.text: Biscuit you'll get a lot out of?

blocks.clueFragment: Biscuit you'll get a lot out of?
blocks.note: surface reading: a cracker that is very filling or good value
setter's reading: one's lot is one's destiny, and this biscuit contains a slip predicting it

explanation.surface: Recommending a biscuit that gives excellent value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lot' means fate here, as in 'one's lot in life', which is what the paper slip inside the biscuit predicts.
explanation.definitionFit: Served in Chinese restaurants in the West, it is a crisp folded wafer hiding a printed prophecy.

clue.text: Regret route regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters of route

explanation.surface: Someone often sorry about the way they travel.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to be sorry about it, to wish it had not happened.

clue.text: Football team with which the Spanish tied

blocks.note: el is the Spanish for 'the'
scores that are tied are level or even

explanation.surface: A football side with which Spain drew a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A football side fields this many players, so the number is used as a noun for the team.

clue.text: Give no food to celebrity vet, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter of the animal doctor is dropped

blocks.note: a star is a celebrity
taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A famous TV vet is accused of not feeding the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve someone is to deprive them of food until they suffer hunger.
